title: How many lakhs make a billion?
description: A billion is turned into crore, and each crore is turned into lakh. The product of the two hundreds gives the number of lakhs, and a multiplication check brings back the billion.
teaching_notes: One idea: change units one step at a time, billion to crore to lakh, since each step multiplies by a hundred. Watch for students who count zeros and lose one.

source: How many lakhs make a billion?
video_script.why: The child knows that a crore is a hundred lakh, and now changes a billion into lakhs step by step.
video_script.substitution: Turn the billion into crore, then each crore into lakh, and multiply the two hundreds.
video_script.anchor: a billion card on the left, a lakh card on the right, and a question mark between them
video_script.payoff_line: Turn the billion into crore, then turn each crore into lakh

final_answer.spoken: ten thousand lakhs make a billion

maths_rules: a lakh is 100 thousand; a crore is 100 lakh; a billion is 100 crore
check: 10,000 x 1,00,000 = 1,00,00,00,000 = 100 crore, which is 1 followed by 9 zeros
video_script.design: One idea: change units one step at a time. The billion and lakh cards stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the two steps and a check. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It uses two big units that we meet in large numbers, a lakh and a billion.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>How many lakhs make up one billion?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A lakh is a hundred thousand, and the next unit up is the crore.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A crore is a hundred lakh, so it is a hundred times a lakh.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each unit here is a hundred times the unit before it, all the way to the billion.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, one billion, and the fact that one crore is a hundred lakh.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many lakhs make 1 billion

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find how many lakhs make up one billion.

marks.m1: the billion card is turned into crore

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, we put the billion in crore.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One billion is the same amount as a hundred crore.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 1 crore = 100 lakh; 100 crore = 100 x 100 lakh = 10,000 lakh
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, we put each crore in lakh, since a crore is a hundred lakh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A hundred crore is then a hundred times a hundred lakh.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A hundred times a hundred is ten thousand, so we get ten thousand lakh.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check: 10,000 x 1,00,000 = 1,00,00,00,000 = 100 crore, which is 1 followed by 9 zeros

marks.m3: the 9 zeros are counted under the number

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, we check by multiplying ten thousand by one lakh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That makes a hundred crore, which is one followed by nine zeros.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This is the same billion we started with, so the answer holds.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Turn the billion into crore, then turn each crore into lakh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten thousand lakhs make a billion.
